mainTopic: The source for the one-third growth rule that decides which year grain belongs to, and whether חכמים can measure one-third precisely
overview: The גמרא is looking for the source that grain belongs to the year in which it reached a third of its growth. It first proves this from "וחג האסיף בצאת השנה": "אסיף" means harvest, and grain harvested on סוכות already reached a third before ראש השנה, yet the Torah ties it to the old year. רבי ירמיה asks whether חכמים can really tell a third from slightly less. רבי זירא answers that all measures of חכמים are exact cut-offs, like a מקוה of forty סאה or a כביצה of food. רבי ירמיה then tries to prove the point from the first עומר brought by ישראל, which came from grain that had not reached a third while a גוי owned it. The גמרא pushes back: maybe that grain had not grown at all, which is easy to see. An argument from the five days between crossing the ירדן and the עומר is knocked down by ארץ צבי, because the land's produce ripens fast. Then רבי חנינא shows that "אסיף" near סוכות refers to threshing-floor waste, not harvest, and רבי זירא admits the proof has been cut down. The גמרא begins a new source from רבי יונתן בן יוסף, "ועשת את התבואה לשלש השנים", which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means grain that did not grow at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading that the verse refers to grain that reached a third in the seventh year. Perhaps it means grain that did not grow at all, and the Torah simply extends שביעית until סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the grain did not grow in the seventh year at all, and still the Torah is telling us: keep the laws of שמיטה going all the way until סוכות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the proof it just brought. It asks whether the verse about סוכות really refers to grain that reached a third in the seventh year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reading said the mention of סוכות teaches that grain which reached a third before ראש השנה stays שביעית produce. This challenge offers another reading: the Torah might be extending שביעית laws until סוכות for all produce, even produce that never grew in the seventh year. If that were true, the ״שליש״ rule would have no source.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps, which opens a challenge
Entered. Here it means the grain reached a third of its growth inside the seventh year
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳
You shall release, meaning keep the laws of שמיטה

steps.confusionAlert: "לא עייל כלל" does not mean the grain does not exist. It means the grain did not reach the one-third growth mark during the seventh year, so it would normally belong to the eighth year.

phrases.english: But perhaps it did not enter [into growth in the seventh year] at all,
phrases.notes: Meaning the grain had not yet reached a third before ראש השנה.

phrases.english: and the Merciful One is saying
keep releasing [observe שמיטה] and continue until the festival of Sukkot!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation that came on the previous amud, which read "בחג הסוכות" as referring to grain that reached a third in the seventh year.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the verse's mention of סוכות refers to grain that reached a third before ראש השנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse could just as easily be a flat extension of שביעית until סוכות for all produce, even produce that never grew in the seventh year. So it does not prove a ״שליש״ rule.

steps.title: Rejecting the challenge by quoting a new verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge and brings the verse "וחג האסיף בצאת השנה" as the basis of its answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that! For it is written: "And the festival of gathering, at the going out of the year."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the challenge and quotes a verse. This is a setup: the next steps explain how the verse proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depends on two parts of the phrase "חג האסיף בצאת השנה". The word "אסיף" needs to be defined, and "בצאת השנה" (the year going out) links סוכות time back to the previous year. The גמרא will now work through what "אסיף" means.

keyTerms.meaning: It should not enter your mind, meaning that idea is wrong
The festival of gathering, another name for סוכות
At the going out (end) of the year

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind, for it is written:
"And the festival of gathering, at the going out of the year"
phrases.notes: שמות כ״ג:ט״ז

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New verse brought to pin down the meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mention of סוכות might simply extend שביעית for all produce.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse "חג האסיף בצאת השנה" will show that it refers to grain connected to the previous year.

steps.title: What does the word אסיף mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what "אסיף" means. It suggests a first option: a festival that comes at the time of gathering the crops.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "אסיף" mean? If you say it means a festival that comes at the season of gathering in crops...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the key word and tries out a first explanation. This is a setup: that explanation is about to be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple meaning of "אסיף" would be the gathering season, when crops are brought in from the field. The גמרא raises this option only to test it. The next step shows that it cannot be the meaning here.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, which introduces a suggestion that will be tested
Gathering in the crops from the field into the house

phrases.english: What is "gathering"?
If you say: a festival that comes at the time of gathering —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the verse brought in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The precise meaning of the word "אסיף" in the verse.

steps.title: That meaning would be repetitive
steps.stepSummary: The first meaning cannot be right, because the same verse already says "באספך" (when you gather), so "אסיף" would be extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the verse already says "when you gather"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first meaning of "אסיף" because the verse would be saying the same thing twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full verse says "וחג האסיף בצאת השנה באספך את מעשיך מן השדה". If "אסיף" only meant the gathering season, the word "באספך" would already teach it. The Torah does not repeat itself for nothing, so "אסיף" must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written! This points out that a verse already says it
When you gather in, from the same verse

phrases.english: but it is written: "when you gather in"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested meaning raised in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the first suggested meaning of "אסיף".
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It makes the word redundant, since "באספך" in the same verse already says it.

steps.title: אסיף means harvesting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that "אסיף" here means קציר, the harvesting (cutting) of grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does "אסיף" mean? Harvesting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of "אסיף": cutting the grain in the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "באספך" refers to bringing the crops into the house. "אסיף" refers to an earlier stage, cutting the grain. So the verse speaks of grain that is still being harvested at סוכות time.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which introduces the correct answer after a rejected one
Harvesting, cutting standing grain

phrases.english: Rather, what is "gathering"? Harvesting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct definition after step 4 rejected the first one.

steps.title: Grain harvested on סוכות belongs to the old year
steps.stepSummary: חכמים know that grain harvested on סוכות must have reached a third before ראש השנה. The Torah calls this time "the going out of the year", which shows such grain is linked to the previous year. This answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis have it established that any grain harvested on סוכות certainly reached a third of its growth before ראש השנה. Yet the Torah calls that time "the going out of the year", meaning it still counts as part of the year that just ended.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. Grain harvested at סוכות already reached a third before ראש השנה, and the Torah ties it to the old year by saying "בצאת השנה".
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though סוכות falls after ראש השנה, the Torah describes it as the end of the old year when speaking of this harvest. That teaches that grain which reached a third in the old year is still governed by that year. So the mention of סוכות in the שמיטה verse refers to grain that reached a third in the seventh year, not to grain that never grew then.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis have it established, an accepted tradition or knowledge
One third, the growth stage at which grain counts for that year
It is certainly known
Grain

steps.whatToRemember: Grain that reached a third of its growth before ראש השנה belongs to the old year. That is why grain that reached a third in the seventh year keeps the laws of שביעית even when it is harvested in the eighth year. The source is "וחג האסיף בצאת השנה", where "אסיף" means harvest.
steps.whyThisMatters: The one-third mark is a basic rule of agricultural הלכה. It decides which year produce belongs to for שביעית, and in related areas such as מעשרות.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis have it established
that any grain that is harvested on the festival [סוכות]
is known to have reached one-third [of its growth]
before ראש השנה,
and [the Torah] calls it "at the going out of the year."
phrases.notes: The harvest time is linked to the year that just ended.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקִים לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן דְּכׇל תְּבוּאָה שֶׁנִּקְצְרָה בֶּחָג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the definition from step 5 to complete the answer to step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Grain that reached a third before ראש השנה is treated as belonging to the old year. So the שמיטה verse's mention of סוכות refers to grain that reached a third in the seventh year.

steps.title: Can חכמים really tell a third from less than a third?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא whether חכמים can really tell the exact difference between grain that reached one-third and grain that reached slightly less.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: Are the Rabbis really able to know the difference between exactly a third and just under a third?
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion opens. רבי ירמיה challenges the practicality of the one-third rule just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole rule depends on a precise cut-off. A tiny difference in growth would place the grain in a different year with very different laws. רבי ירמיה asks how anyone could be sure of such a fine line.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא known for asking sharp, boundary-testing questions
רבי ירמיה's teacher, a leading אמורא
Less than a third

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
And do the Rabbis know for certain
[the difference] between a third and less than a third?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא: וְקִים לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the precision of the one-third rule stated in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reliance on an exact one-third growth mark.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such a fine difference seems impossible to detect, so how can a halacha depend on it?

steps.title: All measurements of חכמים are exact cut-offs
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells רבי ירמיה not to step outside the framework of halacha. Every measurement חכמים set is an exact boundary like this.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't I tell you not to take yourself outside the bounds of הלכה? All the measurements of חכמים are like this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers that this question applies to every measurement in הלכה. The precise cut-off is simply how the measures of הלכה work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many הלכות depend on an exact amount. For example, a מקוה of forty סאה is valid, but forty סאה minus a tiny bit is not. The fact that the line is very fine does not undo the rule. Once חכמים set a measure, it is the boundary, and we do not reopen it with "what about just slightly less?"

keyTerms.meaning: Do not take yourself outside of הלכה. Stay within its accepted framework
The measurements set by חכמים
It is so, meaning they all work this way

steps.whatToRemember: Measurements in הלכה are exact boundaries. Even a tiny difference changes the law, and that is the nature of every measure set by חכמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general principle across all of הלכה (שיעורים). Precise measurements are binding, even when the difference seems tiny.

phrases.english: He said to him: Did I not tell you
do not take yourself outside of the halacha?
All the measurements of the Sages are like this.
phrases.notes: They are exact cut-offs, e.g., a מקוה of forty סאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אָמֵינָא לָךְ לָא תַּפֵּיק נַפְשָׁךְ לְבַר מֵהִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle about how halachic measurements work
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A rule depending on an undetectably fine difference seems unworkable.
steps.terutzMaskana: All rabbinic measures are exact boundaries, so the one-third rule is no different.

steps.title: Examples of exact halachic measurements
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא finishes his point with three examples. In each one, the full measure works in halacha, and even a tiny bit less does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person can immerse in a מקוה of forty סאה, but not in forty סאה missing even a tiny קורטוב. A כביצה of food passes on טומאת אוכלין, but a כביצה missing even a sesame seed does not. A cloth three by three טפחים can become טמא מדרס, but if it is missing even one thread, it cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא is still answering רבי ירמיה. He gives examples to show that חכמים's measurements are exact cutoffs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה doubted that anyone can tell exactly when grain reaches a third of its growth. רבי זירא answers that this is how all measurements in הלכה work. A tiny difference, like a קורטוב, a sesame seed, or one thread, decides the הלכה. So the cutoff of one-third is not stranger than any other measurement.

keyTerms.meaning: Forty סאה, the minimum amount of water for a kosher מקוה
A tiny liquid measure, a very small amount
The size of an egg, the minimum amount of food that can pass on טומאה
Ritual impurity of food
A sesame seed, a tiny amount
Impurity caused when a זב or similar person treads, sits, or leans on an item

steps.whatToRemember: In הלכה, measurements are exact boundaries. Even the smallest amount below the measure changes the law.

phrases.english: In forty se'ah one immerses,
in forty se'ah lacking a kortov —
phrases.notes: A קורטוב is a tiny liquid measure.

phrases.english: he cannot immerse in them.
An egg-bulk makes food impure,
an egg-bulk lacking a sesame seed —
does not make food impure.
A cloth three by three handbreadths can become impure through treading,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה חָסֵר נִימָא אַחַת —
phrases.english: three by three lacking one thread —
cannot become impure through treading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי זירא's answer from step 8 by giving concrete examples.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that halachic measurements are exact cutoffs, so the one-third rule for grain is valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Known הלכות of מקוה, טומאת אוכלין, and מדרס, each with an exact minimum measure.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה takes back his question
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says that his question was not a real problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: Later, רבי ירמיה said: what I said is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה withdraws his own question about whether חכמים can tell when grain reaches a third. This line sets up the proof he is about to bring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רבי ירמיה doubted that חכמים could tell when grain reached a third of its growth. Now he says the question has no basis. He will show it from a question the חברייא once asked רב כהנא.

keyTerms.meaning: Then he said, or he later said. This often signals a change of mind.
What I said is nothing. It is a way of retracting a statement.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya then said:
What I said is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא דַּאֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The person who asked the question in step 7 now drops it himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The question of whether חכמים can measure one-third growth has no basis.

steps.title: Where did the first עומר in ארץ ישראל come from?
steps.stepSummary: The חברייא asked רב כהנא where ישראל got grain for the עומר when they first entered the land. Grain that grew under a גוי does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: The colleagues asked רב כהנא: the עומר that ישראל brought when they entered the land, where did they bring it from? If you say it grew while the land belonged to a גוי, the Torah says "your harvest," and not the harvest of a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה quotes an old question asked to רב כהנא. He is setting up a proof that חכמים do judge whether grain reached one-third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When ישראל entered, the grain in the fields had grown while the land still belonged to the כנענים. The פסוק "קצירכם" means the עומר must come from a Jew's harvest, not a גוי's harvest. So it is unclear what grain could be used.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering of new barley brought on the 16th of ניסן
The colleagues, the group of scholars in the study hall
When they entered the land, in the days of יהושע
Your harvest. The Torah's word that teaches the עומר must come from a Jew's harvest.

steps.confusionAlert: This looks like a new topic, but it is not. רבי ירמיה is building a proof for his retraction. The answer to this question will depend on grain reaching one-third.

phrases.english: For the colleagues asked Rav Kahana:
The omer that the Jewish people offered
when they entered the land,
from where did they offer it?
If you say it was grain that grew in the possession of a gentile,
the Merciful One said "your harvest" —
and not the harvest of a gentile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that will support רבי ירמיה's retraction in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which grain the first עומר in ארץ ישראל could come from, since grain that grew under a גוי is not allowed.

steps.title: Maybe they never brought a עומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the question itself. How do we know they brought a עומר at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know they offered it? Maybe they did not offer it!
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering, the גמרא attacks the assumption behind the question. If no עומר was brought that year, there is nothing to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question "where did they get it" assumes a עומר was brought. The גמרא suggests that maybe, since no proper grain existed, they skipped it that year.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
Perhaps

phrases.english: From where do we know that they offered it?
Perhaps they did not offer it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind the question in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that ישראל brought a עומר when they entered the land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no עומר was brought, the question of where its grain came from disappears.

steps.title: A verse in יהושע proves they brought the עומר
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says they ate new grain only from the day after פסח. This shows they first brought the עומר and only then ate.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not think so, because it is written: "And they ate from the grain of the land on the day after פסח." On the day after פסח they ate. Before that, they did not eat. This is because they offered the עומר and then ate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion that no עומר was brought. It proves from a פסוק in ספר יהושע that they did bring it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New grain is forbidden until the עומר is brought on the 16th of ניסן. The פסוק stresses that they ate only from the day after פסח and not before. That timing only makes sense if they waited to bring the עומר first.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not even think that
The grain of the land
On the day after פסח, the 16th of ניסן
Before, at first

phrases.english: Do not think so, for it is written:
"And they ate from the grain of the land
on the day after Passover."
phrases.notes: יהושע 5:11

phrases.english: On the day after Passover, they ate;
before that, they did not eat.
Because they offered the omer and then ate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe no עומר was brought in the first year.
steps.terutzMaskana: A עומר was brought, because they waited until after the 16th of ניסן to eat new grain.

steps.title: The question returns: where did they bring it from?
steps.stepSummary: Now that we know a עומר was brought, the original question is back. Where did the grain come from?
steps.simpleTranslation: From where did they offer it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the original question, which is now even stronger. This sets up the answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 12 was rejected, so we know a עומר was brought. Grain from a גוי's harvest is not allowed, so the גמרא still needs to explain what grain was used.

keyTerms.meaning: From where?

phrases.english: From where did they offer it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 13 confirms a עומר was brought, the גמרא returns to the question of step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What grain was used for the first עומר, given that a גוי's harvest does not count.

steps.title: Grain that did not reach one-third under a גוי is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that any grain that had not reached one-third of its growth while a גוי owned it was fit for the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: anything that did not reach one-third of its growth while in a גוי's possession.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the question from Step 14. The grain they used was grain that had not yet reached one-third of its growth while a גוי owned it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain grown under a גוי is disqualified only if it reached one-third of its growth while he owned it. If it reached that point only after ישראל took the land, it counts as Jewish grain. This answer assumes someone could tell which stalks had reached one-third and which had not.

keyTerms.meaning: One-third, the growth stage at which grain counts as 'grown' for הלכה
Reached one-third of its full growth
In the possession of a גוי (non-Jew)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: כׇּל שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא שְׁלִישׁ
phrases.english: He said to them: anything that did not reach one-third
phrases.notes: רב כהנא is answering the חברייא.

phrases.english: in the possession of a gentile.
phrases.notes: Such grain was fit for the עומר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question restated in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where did the grain for the first עומר come from?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From grain that had not reached one-third of its growth while a גוי owned it.

steps.title: So the חכמים can tell whether grain reached one-third
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה finishes his proof. If they relied on the one-third rule back then, they must have been able to tell. So today too the חכמים can tell.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the grain had reached one-third and they could not tell? Rather, you must say they could tell. Here too, they can tell.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה uses רב כהנא's answer to prove that experts can tell whether grain reached one-third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא's answer only works if people could tell grain under one-third apart from grain past one-third. If they could not tell, they could not have relied on that rule. Since they did rely on it, they could tell. That same ability applies to our case of grain that reached one-third before ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
Literally 'entered'; here, the grain had grown (reached one-third)
They know for certain; they can tell
Here too; the same applies in our case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'וְדִלְמָא עָיֵיל וְלָא קִים לְהוּ' as a real challenge. It is a rhetorical question, asked only to be rejected. It builds the proof that they could tell.

phrases.english: But perhaps it had grown (to one-third)
phrases.notes: A rhetorical possibility.

phrases.english: and they could not tell?
phrases.notes: If they could not tell, how could they rely on the rule?

phrases.english: Rather, they could tell.
phrases.notes: This is the necessary conclusion.

phrases.english: Here too, they can tell.
phrases.notes: The proof is applied to our question about one-third before ראש השנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רב כהנא's answer into proof of רבי ירמיה's claim from Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The חכמים can tell whether grain has reached one-third of its growth.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב כהנא's ruling that the first עומר came from grain that had not reached one-third under a גוי.

steps.title: Maybe that grain had not grown at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Perhaps the grain had not grown at all under the גוי, which is easy to see. That does not prove the חכמים can tell one-third from slightly less.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it had not grown at all. However, where it reached one-quarter, they cannot tell the difference between one-third and less than one-third!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof. Maybe the case back then was an easy one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the grain had not even sprouted when ישראל arrived, anyone could see it had not reached one-third. That says nothing about hard cases, like grain at one-quarter, where telling one-third from just under one-third is difficult. So the proof may not reach our question.

keyTerms.meaning: Had not grown at all
One-quarter (of its growth)
Less than one-third

phrases.english: But perhaps it had not grown at all,
phrases.notes: An easy, obvious case.

phrases.english: but where it reached one-quarter,
phrases.notes: A hard, borderline case.

phrases.english: between one-third and less than one-third
they cannot tell!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to weaken the proof in Step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the first עומר, not the claim itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof may come from an easy case (no growth at all), which does not show skill in hard borderline cases.

steps.title: Grain cannot ripen from nothing in five days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the pushback. ישראל crossed the ירדן on the tenth of ניסן, and the עומר was cut on the night of the sixteenth. Grain cannot grow from nothing to ripeness in five days. So it had grown partly, and they could still tell whether it reached one-third.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not think so. It is written: 'And the people came up from the ירדן on the tenth of the month.' If you think it had not grown at all, could it have become fully grown in five days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי ירמיה's proof using a פסוק that dates ישראל's arrival in the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישראל arrived on the tenth of ניסן, and the עומר was harvested right after פסח, about five days later. Grain cannot sprout and fully ripen in that time, so it had already grown somewhat under the גוי. Even so, they could tell whether it had passed one-third, so the חכמים can make that call in hard cases too.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not think that; that idea is rejected
On the tenth of the month (ניסן)
Became full, fully ripe

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the five-days argument seems to save רבי ירמיה's proof. But this is only temporary: steps 19–20 show that the five-days argument fails because of ארץ צבי, so the proof from the first עומר is rejected in the end.
steps.confusionAlert: Why 'five days'? From the tenth of ניסן, the days in between (11th through 15th) come to about five before the עומר was cut on the night of the sixteenth. The point is that this is far too short for grain to sprout and fully ripen.

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind,
phrases.notes: The pushback in Step 17 is rejected.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And the people came up from the Jordan
phrases.notes: יהושע 4:19

phrases.english: on the tenth of the month,'
phrases.notes: The tenth of ניסן.

phrases.english: and if it enters your mind
that it had not grown at all,
could it become fully grown in five days?
phrases.notes: Impossible, so the grain had partly grown before ישראל arrived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the pushback in Step 17 and restores the proof in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual proof from a פסוק's timeline.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps the grain had not grown at all, an easy case that proves nothing about borderline cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: The grain must have partly grown under the גוי, yet they could tell it had not reached one-third. So the חכמים can tell even in borderline cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the strongest attempt to save the proof from the first עומר. Watch how the next two steps take it apart.

steps.title: Even partial growth cannot ripen in five days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the five-days argument. Even if the grain had grown a quarter or a sixth, it still could not fully ripen in only five days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what are you saying? That the grain had grown a quarter or a sixth? Even so, can it become fully ripe in five days?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns against the argument from step 18. Saying the grain was partly grown does not fix the timing problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 argued that grain cannot go from nothing to ripe in five days, so it must have been partly grown. But grain that is only a quarter or a sixth grown also cannot ripen in five days by normal nature. So the five-days argument proves nothing either way.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter (of the grain's growth)
A sixth (a small fraction of growth)
Still / even so
Becomes full, meaning fully ripe

phrases.english: Rather, what [are you saying]?
That it had reached a quarter or a sixth [of its growth]?
Still, in five days
can it become fully ripe?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי, דְּעָיֵיל רִבְעָא אוֹ דַנְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the five-days argument of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 18 that five days proves the grain was already partly grown.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Partly grown grain also cannot ripen naturally in five days, so the timing problem exists either way and proves nothing.

steps.title: The land of the deer ripens fast, so the pushback stands
steps.stepSummary: The answer to the timing problem must be that ארץ ישראל is called ארץ צבי, meaning its grain ripens as fast as a deer. If so, the grain could have grown from nothing, and the pushback from step 17 is restored.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? It is written about ארץ ישראל, 'the land of the deer' (it ripens quickly). Here too, 'the land of the deer' is written about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the grain could ripen in five days at all. ארץ ישראל is called ארץ צבי because its produce ripens very fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we need this special speed anyway, it works just as well for grain that had not grown at all under the גוי. So step 17's pushback stands. The grain may have been ungrown, which is easy to see, and רבי ירמיה's proof that the חכמים can tell one-third from slightly less falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Land of the deer', a name for ארץ ישראל implying that its fruit ripens as swiftly as a deer runs
You must say / you are forced to say
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: The five-days argument fails. Fast ripening in ארץ ישראל explains everything, so the grain may have been ungrown. רבי ירמיה's proof that the חכמים can measure one-third is rejected.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase ארץ צבי is not answering for רבי ירמיה. It undoes his defense and brings back the pushback from step 17.

phrases.english: Rather, what must you say?
'The land of the deer' is written about it.
Here too,
'the land of the deer' is written about it.
phrases.notes: So even ungrown grain could have ripened in five days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the timing problem raised in step 19, and in doing so brings back the pushback of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to a special quality of ארץ ישראל: its produce ripens unusually fast.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Five days was too short for ungrown grain, so the grain must have been partly grown and judged by the one-third rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Five days is enough in ארץ צבי even for ungrown grain, so no proof can be drawn about measuring one-third.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The five-days argument fails because ארץ צבי explains fast ripening even for ungrown grain. So the first עומר does not prove that חכמים can tell one-third from slightly less.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: אסיף means gathering leftovers, not harvesting
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא attacks the earlier proof from חג האסיף. He shows that 'gathering' near סוכות refers to collecting threshing-floor and winepress waste, not harvesting grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא objected: Can you really say this 'אסיף' means harvest? Isn't it written, 'when you gather from your threshing floor and from your winepress,' and the Master said that the verse speaks of the waste of the threshing floor and winepress?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier proof for the one-third rule, which was built on calling סוכות חג האסיף, the harvest festival. רבי חנינא challenges that reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof assumed that אסיף means harvesting grain at סוכות time. That would show grain is counted by the year in which it reached one-third. רבי חנינא points to a parallel verse that the חכמים explain as the straw and leftovers used for the סוכה roof. So אסיף is not harvesting, and the proof loses its base.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objects to it
Gathering (the name חג האסיף for סוכות)
Harvest
Waste of the threshing floor and winepress, used as סכך

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina strongly objected to it:
Can you really say
that this 'gathering' means harvesting?
But isn't it written:
'When you gather from your threshing floor and from your winepress'
and the Master said:
The verse speaks of the waste of the threshing floor and winepress!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי ירמיה's argument and returns to the earlier verse-based proof for the one-third rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier proof that reads אסיף at סוכות as harvesting grain.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A parallel verse about gathering at סוכות is explained as threshing-floor leftovers, so אסיף does not mean harvest.

steps.title: רבי זירא: The proof has been cut down
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא admits that רבי חנינא's objection destroyed a proof they had thought was solid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: We had this matter firmly in our hands, and רבי חנינא came and threw an axe at it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא accepts רבי חנינא's objection. The חג האסיף proof is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the objection an axe means the proof is not just weakened but fully chopped down. That leaves the one-third rule without a source, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Was in our hands, meaning we thought it was settled
Threw an axe at it, meaning he chopped down the proof

steps.whatToRemember: The חג האסיף proof for the one-third rule is rejected. A new source is needed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
This matter was in our hands,
and Rabbi Chanina came
and threw an axe at it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: הָא מִילְּתָא הֲוַאי בִּידַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the objection of step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof from חג האסיף is fully rejected.

steps.title: Then where do we learn the one-third rule?
steps.stepSummary: With the old proof gone, the גמרא asks for a new source for the one-third rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a new source. This short question sets up the next move, a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that grain belongs to the year in which it reached one-third of its growth. That rule is still accepted, but its source is gone. The גמרא now looks for a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?

phrases.english: Rather, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the collapse of the proof in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that grain belongs to the year in which it reached one-third growth.

steps.title: רבי יונתן בן יוסף begins with the three-years verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא from רבי יונתן בן יוסף. It begins by quoting the verse promising that the land will give produce 'for three years.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יונתן בן יוסף says: 'And it shall make the produce for three years.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer with a ברייתא. Its verse comes from the שמיטה blessing, and the explanation continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse promises that the sixth-year crop will last for three years. רבי יונתן בן יוסף will read the word 'three' closely to derive the one-third rule. On this amud, only the verse itself has been quoted.
